headline: High risk of cascading errors and data leakage from Khoj-to-unstructured document pipelines; prompt-injection risk is lower but present via shared document content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and unstructured reads documents; if unstructured outputs are fed back into Khoj or copied into its retrieval corpus, attacker-controlled document text can influence downstream instructions. The pair lacks a documented provenance filter, so the shared document channel is the plausible bridge.
conditions: IF unstructured output is ingested into Khoj's indexed notes without provenance tagging
IF a document contains instruction-like text that Khoj later treats as trusted retrieval context
mitigations: Add a provenance prefix to all unstructured outputs before indexing
Manually review one sample document for instruction-like payloads
Disable automatic ingestion from unstructured into Khoj for sensitive folders
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary metadata between the tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, while unstructured reads and writes documents and has allowlisted network egress. If both operate on the same workspace, sensitive content can flow from Khoj-managed notes into unstructured processing and then out through its API calls or logs. No shared-workspace isolation is documented.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same document directory
IF unstructured sends document contents to a remote service during processing
IF Khoj indexes notes that contain secrets or personal data
mitigations: Separate the two agents onto different folders
Process one non-sensitive test document first
Turn off remote processing paths in unstructured where possible
Restrict Khoj indexing to a redacted corpus
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls and audit logging

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj can read files and maintains a shared index across user clients; unstructured can read and write files and spawn subprocesses. If both are pointed at the same directory or index, they can overwrite or race on mutable artifacts. The profiles do not show locking or coordination primitives, so conflict is plausible in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same output directory or index
IF multiple instances of either agent run concurrently on the same workspace
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Run a single instance of each agent during testing
Check for file collisions after one sample run
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj produces retrieval/chat outputs from indexed documents, and unstructured is a document-processing pipeline that can consume those outputs as inputs. If unstructured treats Khoj-generated text as authoritative, extraction or downstream actions can propagate hallucinations or malformed citations into documents at scale. The pair lacks a verification step in the profiles, so the default interaction is risky.
conditions: IF unstructured ingests Khoj-generated summaries or citations as source text
IF downstream workflows act on unstructured outputs without human review
mitigations: Require human review before any downstream action
Feed unstructured only original source documents, not Khoj summaries
Compare one extracted sample against the source file
requires-engineering: add verification and provenance checks between generation and processing

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents, while unstructured processes documents and images. If the pair is used on regulated or residency-sensitive data, the profiles do not show matching retention, residency, or subject-rights controls. Because both are docs-only and no DPA or policy alignment is documented, compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is placed into both agents
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the processed documents
mitigations: Classify the data before processing
Keep regulated documents out of the pair
Review each vendor privacy policy manually
requires-engineering: align retention, residency, and deletion workflows across both systems
